catalyst.event: September CPI released Tue 2026-10-14 08:30 ET (BLS schedule, fetched), then the FOMC decision 2026-10-28 14:00 ET (Fed calendar, fetched). Gold miners trade off real rates, and these are the two dated events that move the real rate inside this horizon.
catalyst.action: accumulate the 90.00-92.20 shelf BEFORE the 10-14 print rather than chasing the reaction; trim a third into the 20-day if it gets there first. Do not add on the print itself.

thesis: The miners are outperforming the metal and that gap is operating leverage showing up in the tape: GDX has beaten GLD by 15.32% over three months and 14.52% over six, and GDX at 92.87 is above its 50-day at 90.01 while GLD at 393.41 is below both its own averages. Cost lines are fixed while the realised gold price is not, so a flat-to-firm metal still expands miner margins — which is why the divergence persists rather than closing. With CPI running +0.40% month-over-month against a 3.88% policy rate, the real rate that has been the drag on this complex is thin, and the 10-14 print is the next dated test of it. Entry is a defined three-point support shelf, not a discount off the last print.
key_risk: GDX is a basket of leveraged operators, so the same operating leverage runs in reverse — a renewed leg down in gold takes the miners further than the metal, and GDX fell 20.74% from its own range high while GLD fell 20.06% from its. The specific danger is the long end: if the 10y keeps climbing from 5.18% without CPI accelerating, the real rate rises and the whole complex de-rates regardless of mine economics, which is the mechanism that produced this drawdown in the first place.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that one month already contradicts three: GDX is -9.32% over the last month and has lagged GLD by 2.70% over that window, so the outperformance I am buying may be in the process of unwinding rather than continuing, and buying a pullback in a complex 20% off its high is the classic mistake. I take the point seriously enough to let it set the structure: the entry is capped at 92.20 and explicitly voided by a close under 90.00, so if the one-month trend is the real signal the idea simply stops out or never fills rather than being averaged down. The counter-evidence is that the one-month lag is a pullback INTO the 50-day while the three- and six-month leads are moves ABOVE it — the shorter window is noise around a level the longer windows built.

catalyst.action: sell the existing long at Monday 2026-09-28 open

thesis: Exit of the long opened 2026-08-18 at 94.00, now 84.51 (-10.1%). LCI supplies components into RVs and towables — the most credit-sensitive big-ticket discretionary category there is — and the fetched rate picture has moved against it, with the 10y at 5.18% versus a 3.88% policy rate. The tape agrees: 84.51 is 43.01% below the 148.30 range high and only 2.10% above the 82.775 range low, with price 8.9% under the 20-day (92.76) and 15.7% under the 50-day (100.28). There were ZERO open-market insider purchases in six months, and the most recent quarter MISSED by 3.60% after three beats. The position has no stop, so absent a decision nothing closes it.
key_risk: Selling a cyclical at 43% off its high is often selling the bottom of the cycle, and the one piece of counter-evidence is real: sell-side bullish share is 61.1% and improving (+2.3pp), so the professionals covering it are getting more positive, not less. If the RV cycle troughs here this exit will look like capitulation at the low.
counter_argument: The strongest case to hold is the cycle argument plus the improving revisions: RV demand is famously early-cycle, a 43% drawdown prices a lot of bad news, and buying the trough requires enduring exactly this. What answers it is the absence of any confirmation that the trough is here — no insider bought a single share in six months, which is the cheapest signal management could have sent and did not; the last print was a miss; and price is making lower lows beneath both averages rather than basing. Improving analyst sentiment against a falling price is the weakest of the three confirmations available and the only one present. A cycle call with no stop, no dated catalyst and no insider support is a hope, and I would rather re-enter on evidence than hold for it.
